properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/08/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/08/2023
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8164961
Permit API: 125-22753
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/08/2023
Comments: On 11/08/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well. The following was observed:Operator and well information on site (Photos 1, 2). I recommend placing the rest of the well information on the same sign that has the operator information.Pumpjack in motion upon arrival, some grease/oil on gravel. I recommend removal (Photo 3). Wellhead, production equipment were in generally good condition (Photos 2-5). Mild corrosion. Additional equipment adjacent to the well approximately 40 feet away - there is a depression around the equipment and it is filled with water; dead vegetation around depression, no high conductivity reading. I recommend addressing the depression and exploring the cause of the depression and dead vegetation - unclear if cause if from equipment or pooled water (Photos 6).Downslope of the well were five production tanks within an earthen berm. The berm was in generally good condition, however the pooled water within the berm contained high conductivity readings, specifically in front of tank 1. The sediment within the berm had adequate readings, however the rest of the pooled water had slightly elevated readings. A slightly elevated conductivity reading was taken within the gravel/sediment below the valve of tank 5. This area was relatively small and is recommended that any affected material is removed and disposed of properly. A corroded piece of equipment noted near tank 5 (Photos 7-22, see captions for specific locations). I notified the operator while onsite; a vac truck later was there removing the fluid as I was leaving. Plans are to add equipment to catch fluids when the vac truck removes the hose from the valves. It is noted that the access road has multiple uses, including agricultural, however the access roads to the well sites require routine monitoring and maintenance.Due to the observation of elevated conductivity readings within the pooled water and prompt remediation, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and were immediately corrected. A follow up inspection to ensure there is not residual production fluids within the berm. No additional violations are being issued right now, however additional violations may be forthcoming.

Comments: On June 24, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad.All areas that had been excavated off of the well pad due to the spill have been back filled and regraded. These areas have not been reseeded or temporarily stabilized. The DEP recommends temporarily stabilizing the recently rebuilt infiltration berms and pad slope, if reseeding the area is not planned in the future to prevent accelerated erosion of the area. The DEP also recommends areas of the permitted site that have not achieved the 70% uniform, perennial vegetative covered be reseeded. Two monitoring wells were observed drilled off to the west of the pad about 50 yards. There has not been any remediation of the well pad to date.About 8 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There was about 12 inches of water in the northwest stormwater vault and the water was not high enough in the vault to be able to screen for conductivity with the water quality meter.The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.5 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 20.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 24.2 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 99. 6 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 100.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. Seep 3 was dry and a conductivity screening could not be completed. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 108.1 uS/cm. Seep 5 was dry and a conductivity screening could not be completed. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers.Infiltration berms 4, 6, and 7 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to reported release of diesel fuel. The release occurred on the eastern side of the pad near the pipeline that is run to the site. The release was reported as at least 5 gallons of fuel. The location of the release was not near containment used for the recent drilling onsite. The source and total volume of the release were unknown at the time of inspection.Mr. Dirt was onsite excavating the impacted soil. The initial area marked for excavation was approximately 8' by 10'. The excavation increased to an irregular shape that was about 15' by 20' across and 8' deep. This increase in size was due in part to the stability of the excavated area causing the edges of the pit to break away. The impacted area was also excavated in a manner to ensure the complete removal of impacted soil.The removed material amounted to about 5 loads of soil that were 15 cubic yards per load. The soil was stored on secondary containment for the time being. Creston was also onsite collecting soil samples to verify that the remediation was sufficient.Based on the unknown volume of fuel released it is strongly recommended that Chesapeake remediate the location under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection Violations Noted for 78a56(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b).

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8253362
Permit API: 123-48915
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: A production equipment malfunction at the ANF 194 49 conventional well resulted in a release of crude oil and produced fluids. The Department was notified of the release by Jason Wells of Wilmoth Interests, Inc. The well was shut in from the gathering lines at the time of the malfunction. Therefore, when the malfunction occurred, downhole pressure released vertically from the well head causing crude oil to be sprayed a significant distance above the well before ultimately settling on the well pad and nearby vegetation. The approximate radius of crude oil laden vegetation and forest understory spans 200 feet in every direction from the well head. It appears that the heaviest aerial migration of the release traveled in a southeast to easterly direction from the well. The exact volume of the release is not immediately quantifiable, but it is clearly in excess of the one barrel limit set forth in the Department's spill policy.The bulk of the fluids released settled on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, 3-4 inches of crude oil and produced fluids were present on the pad near the well head. Recent rainfall contributed to the volume of liquid present on the pad, and some stormwater runoff was observed to be flowing down the access road berm and onto the pad. The specific conductance of standing fluid on the pad near the flow of stormwater was found to be 6,080 micro Siemens per centimeter. The specific conductance of standing fluid near the well head was found to be in excess of 20,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. No fluids with elevated specific conductance were observed beyond the well pad at the time of this inspection.The crude oil released on the well pad was observed to have migrated beyond the well pad and downslope in a southern direction. The brush barrier downslope of the well pad was heavily coated with crude oil. Pooled crude oil was observed to have migrated beyond the brush barrier on the forest floor and potentially via porous subsurface material. The extent of pooled crude oil visible on the surface of the forest floor was located at a point approximately 180 feet south/southeast of the well pad.Cleanup efforts began immediately after the release was discovered and brought under control. A ditch was excavated along the downslope end of the well pad to provide containment and a means by which to collect pooled fluids with a vac truck. Jason Wells contacted a consulting firm soon after the release with the intent to retain a consultant to oversee the cleanup process for Wilmoth. I spoke with Jason onsite at the time of this inspection to notify him that violations would be included with the inspection report.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8253362
Permit API: 123-48915
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/23/2025
Comments: A production equipment malfunction at the ANF 194 49 conventional well resulted in a release of crude oil and produced fluids. The Department was notified of the release by Jason Wells of Wilmoth Interests, Inc. The well was shut in from the gathering lines at the time of the malfunction. Therefore, when the malfunction occurred, downhole pressure released vertically from the well head causing crude oil to be sprayed a significant distance above the well before ultimately settling on the well pad and nearby vegetation. The approximate radius of crude oil laden vegetation and forest understory spans 200 feet in every direction from the well head. It appears that the heaviest aerial migration of the release traveled in a southeast to easterly direction from the well. The exact volume of the release is not immediately quantifiable, but it is clearly in excess of the one barrel limit set forth in the Department's spill policy.The bulk of the fluids released settled on the well pad. At the time of this inspection, 3-4 inches of crude oil and produced fluids were present on the pad near the well head. Recent rainfall contributed to the volume of liquid present on the pad, and some stormwater runoff was observed to be flowing down the access road berm and onto the pad. The specific conductance of standing fluid on the pad near the flow of stormwater was found to be 6,080 micro Siemens per centimeter. The specific conductance of standing fluid near the well head was found to be in excess of 20,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. No fluids with elevated specific conductance were observed beyond the well pad at the time of this inspection.The crude oil released on the well pad was observed to have migrated beyond the well pad and downslope in a southern direction. The brush barrier downslope of the well pad was heavily coated with crude oil. Pooled crude oil was observed to have migrated beyond the brush barrier on the forest floor and potentially via porous subsurface material. The extent of pooled crude oil visible on the surface of the forest floor was located at a point approximately 180 feet south/southeast of the well pad.Cleanup efforts began immediately after the release was discovered and brought under control. A ditch was excavated along the downslope end of the well pad to provide containment and a means by which to collect pooled fluids with a vac truck. Jason Wells contacted a consulting firm soon after the release with the intent to retain a consultant to oversee the cleanup process for Wilmoth. I spoke with Jason onsite at the time of this inspection to notify him that violations would be included with the inspection report.A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Comments: On December 7, 2018, the Department performed an inspection of the CNX RHL22 well pad site. The site is located in Richhill Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a follow up inspection related to a reported reuse water release to the well pad on 12/1/18, and violations issued on 12/3/18. The operator initially reported a 30 barrel reuse water release to the well pad @ 01:15 a.m. on 12/1/18. The operator did contact the Department at 11:00 a.m. on 12/1/18 to report that the release was greater and was approximately 210 barrels of reuse water. The operator has reported that during the transfer of reuse water from the constructed MASS on the tank pad, along the access road, to the working tanks a communication error occurred and the working tanks were over filled causing a release of approximately 210 barrels of reuse water to the well pad. The reuse water overwhelmed the well pad secondary containment discharging to the well pad and storm water collection channels for the site. The reuse water then entered the PCSM structure discharging off site. The collection channel to the PCSM was also overwhelmed and the water was discharged onto the RHL28 gathering pipeline ROW adjacent to the well pad site. The operator was excavating impacted material off site on the pipeline ROW at time of inspection. The operator was also excavating the PCSM and PCSM collection channel at time of inspection. The operator was using field conductivity readings to direct the excavation activities. The operator had attempted to plug the PCSM discharge structure, with an inflatable rubber plug, but was unable to do so. The Department observed elevated conductivity readings in the standing water and soils on the southwest corner of the well pad, as well as the storm water controls for this area. Elevated conductivity readings were also observed off the well pad site on the pipeline ROW and down gradient from both sites during the 12/3/18 inspection. The operator has completed hydraulic fracturing operations on the site and has begun removing the equipment necessary for hydraulic fracturing from the well pad. The operator has reported to the Department that secondary containment will be setup on the well pad to store excavated, impacted soils for disposal and remediation efforts will continue all weekend and into next week on the well pad as well as in the PCSM structures impacted by the reuse water spill.

Comments: On May 15, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3944466, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3944466, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2-5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head was not observed on the ground during this inspection. The Department recommended in IR 3944466 that this top hatch be replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Comments: On November 7, 2025, the Department conducted an inspection at the Burkett well site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. This inspection was conducted in response to Stimulation notifications that were submitted by the operator on October 31, 2025. Stimulation operations were scheduled to begin on November 4, 2025, for wells 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, and 11H.An Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP) was terminated for this site on August 12, 2020.The following was observed during this inspection:Upon starting this inspection, the Department spoke with Halliburton representative Phillip Gonzalez, who cautioned the Department about the hazards present on site, such as moving vehicles and high-pressure lines. Wells 1H, 2H, 3H, 4H, 5H, and 11H appear to be undergoing stimulation operations simultaneously at the time of inspection (photos 8 and 9). Five additional well heads are onsite that appear to be in production (photo 7).The old GPU/Vertical Separator Units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (photo 15). However, their associated wells were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. The new GPU/Vertical Separator Units onsite are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 13 and 14). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022. The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (photo 16). All other containers and machinery onsite that appear to store regulated substances are placed within secondary containment (photos 2 and 10). The well pad containment appears to be in good condition at the time of inspection, with no tears observed. Range Resources representative Justin Fedor was onsite during this inspection who provided the secondary containment inspection log upon request (photo 11). No evidence of fluid leaks was observed from the portion of the MCC Partners to Burkett Temporary Waterline (TWL) at the well pad (photo 12). The Act 9 sign is located at the access road entrance and is not obscured from vegetation, in accordance with 78a55 requirements (photo 24). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness and Contingency (PPC) plan, well permits, and safety data sheets are located onsite (photos 17-20). However, the PPC plan is not specific to this site. The ERP appears to contain the sections required by 78a.55. The access road and well pad were muddy during this inspection with little observable gravel (photos 1 and 23). This appears to be causing sedimentation from the access road to occur in the rock-lined channel along the access road (photos 21 and 22). This sedimentation appears to continue downslope for approximately 20 feet along the access road and stops within the boundaries of the well site.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued against the accumulating sediment from the access road in the rock-lined channel.Violations are to be issued in IR 4091983 for failure to have a site-specific PPC plan on site and for failure to maintain the access road which resulted in sedimentation.

Residual waste may not be disposed of at a different well location than from where it was generated. This action violates 25 Pa. Code 250.3(a) and 25 Pa. Code 78.62(a)1. To resolve the 78.62(a)1 violation, all residual waste disposed of in the pit located at the ANF 172 56 OG WELL location must be removed and disposed of at an authorized facility. It is requested that the Department be notified when the pit excavation will occur, so that Department officials may observe the excavation process and the fully excavated pit.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/11/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 964978
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Drilling/Alteration
Inspection Date: 8/11/2022
Comments: On 8/11/2022, DEP representatives John Rogers and Brooke Millisock conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. It was 75 degrees when we arrived on location. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration berms. Infiltration berm 1 is adequately stabilized but infiltration berm 2 does not meet the vegetative requirements.A frac crew was on site, in the process of fracking nine newly drilled wells. These will add to the one completed well already on site. Chesapeake's Josh Lombardo met us upon our arrival and accompanied us on our inspection. The crew had completed the first three wells and were working on the next five wells, zippering between the wells as they were completing the various stages. Wireline had a gun downhole on one well and perfed a stage while we were on location.During the inspection, we witnessed various water puddles and muddy areas around the location that we field tested with an Oakton PCTS 50 and a Hanna Groline soil test probe with the following results:3.36 mS conductance measured in a 4'x20' puddle on the north side of the pad.2.16 mS conductance measured in 30'x30' puddle west of the generators on the north side of the pad.1.449 mS conductance and green staining in a 10'x15' puddle on the northeast side of the fresh water AST.3.02 mS conductance measured in area sprayed for dust control along the east side of the pad. There was a 5'x10' water puddle in a 20'x40' mud area. We were informed that freshwater was being used for dust control.A 2'x8' puddle near the generator adjacent to the company man trailer measured 4.44 mS conductance.An area where a water puddle was identified with over 20.0 mS conductance on a 7/28/2022 inspection has been excavated. Water in this area measured 14.91 mS conductance during today's inspection.We discussed our findings with Josh. He would have a crew member vacuum the various water spots. I discussed the findings with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein who said that when the fracking was complete, Chesapeake would send personnel in to assess the scope of contamination and respond accordingly. Eric also reported that the area containing the high conductance puddle identified during the 7/28/022 inspection had been assessed and a damaged area of the frac operations containment was identified and repaired. The ground in this area was excavated but the contamination not completely removed. Eric said that when fracking operations was completed, the containment would be removed and excavation would continue. The release of high conductance fluid to the pad surface is a violation of CSL 402(b).The DEP recommends the following:1. Because of the high conductance fluid escaping from damaged containment during well stimulation activities, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 due to unknown volume impacting the unprotected pad surface.2. Assess the various areas of elevated conductance to identify possible causes and repair/report as necessary.2. Continue to monitor the stability of infiltration berm 2 and apply additional resources as necessary to achieve the 70% vegetative requirement.We left the site at 12:00 hrs.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that an estimated 5 gallons of produced fluid was released through a hole in a section of secondary containment. It rained heavily during this inspection. Six wells have been drilled and stimulated on the well pad. It appears that flowback operations are complete. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition.A battery of frac tanks is present within secondary containment near the production tanks. The tanks and secondary containment appear to be in good condition. No holes or patches were observed in the containment liner. The containment appeared to be retaining water. The fluid within the containment had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 947 uS/cm. The puddles on the pad surface near the containment had an EC of less than 900 uS/cm. A bucket within the secondary containment had a label on it which says spill waste for disposal. In one corner of the containment, the fluid in the containment had a petroleum sheen on it. A water truck driver arrived during this inspection and began to vacuum out the containment during this inspection. In a phone call with Brett Staller of Repsol, he stated that a water truck driver had dropped a hose on the secondary containment liner for the frac tank battery and created a 4-6 inch hole in the containment. Pad material was excavated beneath the hole and the hole was patched, he stated. I could not see a hole or patch in the liner during this inspection but there was approximately 2 inches of stormwater in the containment at the time due to the heavy rain. The bottom of the liner was also obscured where a petroleum sheen was present on the surface of the stormwater in the southeast corner of the containment. Violations cited and are considered immediately corrected.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/31/2024 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/31/2024
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8212371
Permit API: 083-51666
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/31/2024
Comments: Upon being made aware of a crude oil release near this conventional well, I contacted Pennhills and learned that a steel gathering line located along the eastern side of the road (downslope of this well) was found to be compromised on December 9, 2024 and actions were taken to repair the line and remediate impacted media at that time. Since that time, Pennhills has decommissioned and vac'd out all fluid from the compromised line and are currently using a different gathering line that parallels the western edge of the road to carry fluids from this well and others located beyond this location. Representatives of Pennhills stated that the bulk of the earth disturbance along the eastern edge of the road was conducted to locate the portion of the line that was leaking and that they constructed an underflow dam downslope of the road to contain residual product that continues to leach from the road bank due to the abundance of larger rocks and roots in the area. Upon my arrival for this inspection, I observed the disturbed area along the eastern edge of the road that accesses this well. There was no visual evidence of crude oil across this disturbance, which was temporarily stabilized with seed and mulch. Downslope of the road, an approximate 20'x30' area had soil exposed due to Pennhills' reported removal of oil soaked leaves from the area. Isolated pockets of crude oil remain throughout this area, which drains towards the underflow dam that is located approximately 100' east of the well [41.82619 -78.85691]. The underflow dam is functioning and appears to be regularly maintained, as there is currently only a minor sheen atop the standing water behind it.Crude oil was also observed on the surface at a recessed area approximately 30' east (41.82632 -78.85674 [downslope]) of the underflow dam that appears to have migrated subsurface from the vicinity of the underflow dam to this point.A second area of oil soaked leaves/soil was discovered approximately 30' south (41.82607 -78.85661) of the underflow dam in a currently dry channel.At this time, the constructed underflow dam and continued use of absorbent diapers/booms appear to be sufficient containment measures. It is highly suggested to regularly monitor the containment and evaluate downslope of the impacted area, particularly during and after rain and snowmelt events.The quantity of product released was unknown, but appears to be less than one barrel at this time. No watercourses have impacted by this incident at this time. Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate if the current containment remains sufficient, if there was further migration of crude oil or evidence is presented that indicates the released quantity was greater than one barrel.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Swepi Lp

Violation Date: 2019-08-23
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 859920
Permit API: 117-21808
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-08-23
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted and INCIDENT inspection of the SWEPI LP - Gee 848 Well Pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 8/23/2019 @1145 hours in response to notification of a spill. The weather was 68 degrees, cloudy, 64% humidity, winds WNW @9mph. SWEPI personnel were present onsite assisting in cleanup activities. CTS report#344583 states "April Heater of Shell notified Carrie Knapp (O&G) that approx. 5 gallons of produced water spilled from a separator inside the pack and some of it leaked onto the ground. They discovered it around 8:45 this morning and are in the process of cleanup." As of today's inspection, what appears to be a line related to the separator, for the 23H well, washed out causing production fluid and sand to spray inside of the well pack. The fluid flowed out the side entry door, and the rear entry door, impacting pad material below the doorways. Due to size of the impacted pad areas, after hand removal of superficial material had taken place, and the visual assessment of fluid and sand inside the well pack; it is recommended SWEPI re-evaluate the initial estimate of 5 gallons of fluid released. Onsite personnel stated a vac box was scheduled for delivery for additional waste to be excavated. Secondary containment was delivered during the inspection. Onsite personnel were preparing to power wash the inside of the well pack, while a vac truck removed the wash water from the rear entry door. Cleanup activities were ongoing when I departed the site. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately corrected against the 23H well: CSL 402b SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a57 I departed the site @1245 hours. On 8/26/2019 Pat Bernethy, SWEPI Env Coordinator reported the revised spill volume is 5-10 gallons and the spill has been fully remediated.
